evals.name: full-batch-plan
evals.prompt: I've got a load of PRs piled up on both levelup repos and I don't want 20 separate deploys. Don't merge or push anything yet — I want to see the plan first. What would a batch merge actually land, in what order, and what's most likely to bite us?
evals.expected_output: A plan that enumerates open PRs across BOTH repos, groups them by Linear ticket, flags cross-repo tickets as atomic, orders migration work last, names the Alembic multiple-heads risk and the lockfile risk, states that staging has no CI so the gate is local tests, and stops without pushing.

evals.name: subset-cross-repo
evals.prompt: can you merge PAD-89 and PAD-90 together? plan it out first, I want to see what you'd do before you touch anything
evals.expected_output: Identifies that PAD-89 = backend #57 + frontend #79 and PAD-90 = backend #58 + frontend #80, treats each ticket as atomic across repos, plans staging reset from main, joint E2E test gate, backend-before-frontend merge order, and stops for approval.

evals.name: backend-only-trap
evals.prompt: plan a batch merge of just the open backend PRs — frontend can wait. I'm mainly worried about the migrations breaking the deploy like they did before. don't push anything.
evals.expected_output: Catches that a backend-only batch would land half of several cross-repo tickets (PAD-75, 78, 89, 90, 92, 101) and warns/recommends against it or proposes excluding them. Runs the Alembic head check, explains the multiple-heads outage and the merge-revision fix, and notes a green deploy workflow does not prove prod is healthy.
